findings.problem: fs::read_to_string(path).unwrap() panics on file-not-found or I/O error
findings.failure_mode: Untrusted or missing file path aborts the entire program instead of returning a typed I/O error
findings.fix: Return Result<Vec<Record>, io::Error> and use ? operator, or return a typed domain error

findings.problem: parts[0] uses unchecked indexing on a Vec derived from split
findings.failure_mode: A line with zero commas produces a single-element Vec; indexing [0] is technically safe here but the same pattern on [1] panics
findings.fix: Use split_once(',') to destructure into exactly (before_comma, after_comma) with no indexing

findings.problem: parts[1] uses unchecked indexing; panics if line has fewer than one comma
findings.failure_mode: Malformed input line without a comma causes a panic at runtime instead of a recoverable error
findings.fix: Use split_once(',') and match the tuple; reject lines without exactly one comma with a typed error

findings.failure_mode: A line like 'foo,bar' panics instead of returning a ParseError for the record
findings.fix: Use .parse::<u32>().map_err(|e| ParseError::InvalidValue(e))? with a typed domain error

findings.problem: (u32) as u16 is a lossy cast that silently truncates values above 65535
findings.failure_mode: A valid u32 like 70000 becomes 4416 without any error, corrupting data silently
findings.fix: Use u16::try_from(value) and propagate an overflow error, or validate value <= 65535 before casting

findings.problem: Record.value is pub u16, allowing any caller to construct a Record with an out-of-range value without domain validation
findings.failure_mode: The domain invariant that value must come from a parsed/validated source is not enforced by the type system
findings.fix: Make value private or use a newtype like PubValue(u16) with a fallible constructor, and expose only via accessor

findings.problem: println! is a side-effecting I/O call embedded inside data-parsing logic
findings.failure_mode: Core data logic is coupled to stdout; cannot be tested deterministically, cannot be suppressed in production, mixes shell and core concerns
findings.fix: Remove println! from the parsing function; logging belongs in the imperative shell at the call site

findings.problem: split(',').map(.to_string()).collect() into Vec<String> allocates all parts eagerly when only two fields are needed
findings.failure_mode: Unnecessary heap allocations per line increase memory pressure and GC cost; each field string is cloned twice (into Vec then into Record)
findings.fix: Use line.split_once(',') to get two &str references, then trim each individually without collecting

findings.problem: part.trim().to_string() allocates a String per field when &str would suffice until the final Record construction
findings.failure_mode: Each field is allocated into a heap String inside the intermediate Vec, then cloned again into Record.name
findings.fix: Keep as &str until Record fields are constructed; use split_once to avoid intermediate Vec entirely

findings.problem: load_tokens mixes I/O (fs::read_to_string) with parsing logic in a single function
findings.failure_mode: The pure parsing cannot be unit-tested without touching the filesystem; violates core/shell separation
findings.fix: Split into parse_records(&[str]) -> Result<Vec<Record>, RecordError> (pure core) and load_tokens(path) -> Result<Vec<Record>, Error> (shell that reads and delegates)

findings.problem: No benchmark exists for the token-loading pipeline
findings.failure_mode: Allocation-heavy split+collect pattern has no measured performance baseline; regressions go undetected
findings.fix: Add criterion or divan benchmarks measuring lines-per-second for typical input sizes

missing_evidence: no benchmark exists for the stated performance or allocation characteristics
no profiler data for the hot path
no allocation tracking or second-ring defense evidence
no command-line evidence (cargo fmt, cargo clippy, cargo test) was run
residual_risk: Static review only; multiple BLOCKER-level panics and silent data corruption paths identified but not fixed. No commands executed. The crate as-is will panic on any malformed input, missing file, or out-of-range numeric value, and silently truncates values above u16::MAX.
